relations.myth: Zeus impersonates Amphitryon and lies with Alcmene
relations.note: Zeus deceives Alcmene by assuming Amphitryon’s appearance and fathers Heracles.

relations.myth: Zeus impersonates Amphitryon during the extended night
relations.note: Zeus usurps Amphitryon’s identity, reports his victory, and sleeps with Alcmene.

relations.myth: Divine rain extinguishes Alcmene’s pyre
relations.note: Zeus apparently vindicates Alcmene by sending rain against Amphitryon’s attempted burning.

relations.myth: Zeus orders Alcmene removed to the Blessed Isles
relations.note: Later tradition makes Zeus command Alcmene’s bodily removal and substitution with a stone.

relations.myth: Hera delays Alcmene’s labor
relations.note: Hera restrains Alcmene’s delivery so Eurystheus is born first and gains sovereignty.

relations.myth: Hera sends serpents against the infant twins
relations.note: Hera attacks Alcmene’s household by sending two serpents against Heracles and Iphicles.

relations.myth: Eileithyia magically obstructs Alcmene’s childbirth
relations.note: The birth-goddess prevents Alcmene from delivering until deceived by a female helper.

relations.myth: The Moirai obstruct Alcmene’s delivery
relations.note: The Moirai join Eileithyia in preventing Alcmene from giving birth.

relations.myth: Hecate receives Alcmene’s transformed helper
relations.note: Hecate transforms Galinthias and later makes Alcmene’s helper her sacred attendant.

relations.myth: Mercury assists Jupiter’s impersonation plot
relations.note: Mercury impersonates Sosia and helps Jupiter maintain the deception of Alcmene and Amphitryon.

relations.myth: Hermes carries Alcmene to the Blessed Isles
relations.note: At Zeus’s command, Hermes substitutes a stone and transports Alcmene to the Blessed Isles.

relations.myth: Helios delays sunrise during Zeus’s extended night
relations.note: Zeus orders Helios not to rise while Alcmene is deceived by the divine impersonation.

relations.myth: Selene cooperates in extending Alcmene’s night
relations.note: Some later accounts enlist Selene in the cosmic pause enabling Zeus’s deception.

relations.myth: Night accompanies the extended-night tradition
relations.note: Personified Night is associated with the prolonged night surrounding Alcmene’s conception of Heracles.

relations.myth: Poseidon’s golden hair protects Amphitryon’s enemy
relations.note: Poseidon gives Pterelaus the life-preserving hair that structures Amphitryon’s Taphian war.

relations.myth: Athena stops mad Heracles from killing Amphitryon
relations.note: Athena strikes Heracles unconscious with a stone, saving Amphitryon from his murderous madness.

relations.myth: Delphi decides Alcmene’s burial place
relations.note: Apollo’s oracle resolves the Heracleidae’s dispute by directing that Alcmene be buried at Megara.
Alcmene marries or cohabits with Rhadamanthys after Amphitryon’s death.

relations.myth: Alcmene joins Rhadamanthys in the Blessed Isles
relations.note: A variant places Alcmene’s marriage to Rhadamanthys after her supernatural removal.
Alcmene is Heracles’ biological mother by Zeus.
Amphitryon is Heracles’ social and putative father, expressed by the Homeric patronymic.

relations.myth: Amphitryon teaches Heracles chariot driving
relations.note: Amphitryon acts as Heracles’ benevolent instructor and teaches him to drive a chariot.

relations.myth: Amphitryon fights beside Heracles against the Minyans
relations.note: Amphitryon joins Heracles in battle against the Minyans of Orchomenus.

relations.myth: Heracles returns and saves Amphitryon’s household
relations.note: Heracles returns before Lycus can execute Amphitryon, Megara, and the children.

relations.myth: Mad Heracles nearly kills Amphitryon
relations.note: Hera-driven madness turns Heracles against his household, leaving Amphitryon in mortal danger.
Alcmene and Amphitryon are the biological parents of Iphicles.

relations.myth: Amphitryon tests the twins with serpents
relations.note: Amphitryon endangers Iphicles and Heracles with snakes to determine which infant is his.
Some late genealogies make Laonome the daughter of Amphitryon and Alcmene.
Alcmene is Electryon’s daughter in the mainstream genealogy.

relations.myth: Amphitryon accidentally kills Electryon
relations.note: Amphitryon’s thrown club rebounds from a cow and kills Alcmene’s father.

relations.myth: Amphitryon kills Electryon in anger
relations.note: Fragmentary variants make Electryon’s death intentional rather than accidental.
Pseudo-Apollodorus names Anaxo as Alcmene’s mother.
A variant genealogy names Lysidice as Alcmene’s mother.
Diodorus names Eurydice, daughter of Pelops, as Alcmene’s mother.
Amphitryon is Alcaeus’ son in the standard Perseid genealogy.
One mythographic genealogy names Astydameia as Amphitryon’s mother.
One mythographic genealogy names Laonome as Amphitryon’s mother.
One mythographic genealogy names Hipponome as Amphitryon’s mother.
Alcmene and Amphitryon both descend from Perseus through Electryon and Alcaeus.
Alcmene and Amphitryon are Andromeda’s descendants through the Perseid line.
Asius reportedly made an uncertain or homonymous Alcmene the daughter of Amphiaraus.
Asius reportedly made an uncertain or homonymous Alcmene the daughter of Eriphyle.

relations.myth: Sthenelus expels the couple after Electryon’s death
relations.note: Sthenelus drives Amphitryon, Alcmene, and Licymnius into exile.

relations.myth: Eurystheus’ premature birth displaces Alcmene’s son
relations.note: Hera ensures Eurystheus is born first, depriving Heracles of the promised Perseid sovereignty.

relations.myth: Alcmene mutilates Eurystheus’ severed head
relations.note: Alcmene gouges out the dead Eurystheus’ eyes in vengeance for his persecution of her family.
Licymnius is Alcmene’s surviving half-brother.

relations.myth: Licymnius accompanies Alcmene and Amphitryon into exile
relations.note: Licymnius travels with the couple after Sthenelus expels them.

relations.myth: Creon purifies the exiled Amphitryon
relations.note: Creon receives Amphitryon at Thebes and purifies him after Electryon’s death.

relations.myth: Creon supplies aid for the Taphian expedition
relations.note: After the fox crisis is solved, Creon contributes Theban support to Amphitryon’s campaign.

relations.myth: Teiresias explains Zeus’s visit to Amphitryon
relations.note: Teiresias reveals that Zeus, not Amphitryon, visited Alcmene during the preceding night.

relations.myth: Teiresias interprets Heracles’ serpent victory
relations.note: Teiresias explains the infant’s feat to Alcmene and Amphitryon and foretells his career.

relations.myth: Historis tricks Hera’s agents during Alcmene’s labor
relations.note: Historis falsely announces the birth, causing the Pharmacides to release their obstruction.

relations.myth: Galanthis falsely announces Alcmene’s delivery
relations.note: Alcmene’s helper deceives the obstructing powers, releasing the prolonged labor.

relations.myth: Cephalus joins the fox hunt and Taphian war
relations.note: Amphitryon recruits Cephalus, Laelaps’ owner, for both the fox crisis and expedition.

relations.myth: Amphitryon deploys Laelaps against the Teumessian fox
relations.note: Amphitryon uses the infallible hound to pursue the creature fated never to be caught.

relations.myth: Amphitryon counters the uncatchable Teumessian fox
relations.note: Amphitryon must resolve the fox’s depredations before Creon will support his war.

relations.myth: Panopeus joins Amphitryon’s Taphian expedition
relations.note: Panopeus serves as one of Amphitryon’s allies against the Taphians and Teleboans.

relations.myth: Heleus joins Amphitryon’s Taphian expedition
relations.note: Heleus serves as one of Amphitryon’s allies in the campaign.

relations.myth: Amphitryon wars against Pterelaus
relations.note: Amphitryon attacks Pterelaus’ kingdom but cannot prevail while the king retains his golden hair.

relations.myth: Comaetho betrays Pterelaus for love of Amphitryon
relations.note: Comaetho’s love for Amphitryon leads her to remove her father’s life-preserving hair.

relations.myth: Amphitryon executes Comaetho after victory
relations.note: Amphitryon kills Comaetho as punishment for betraying her father.

relations.myth: Iolaus and Alcmene share the Cynosarges cult group
relations.note: Iolaus receives cult alongside Alcmene, Heracles, and Hebe without a surviving direct exchange.

relations.myth: Hebe and Alcmene share the Cynosarges cult group
relations.note: Hebe receives cult alongside Alcmene, Heracles, and Iolaus without a surviving direct narrative.
Alcmene is Hyllus’ grandmother through Heracles.

relations.myth: Hyllus sends Eurystheus’ head to Alcmene
relations.note: Hyllus delivers Eurystheus’ severed head, enabling Alcmene’s posthumous vengeance.

relations.myth: Amphitryon protects Megara during Lycus’ usurpation
relations.note: Amphitryon remains with his daughter-in-law Megara as Lycus prepares to execute them.

relations.myth: Lycus threatens Amphitryon and Heracles’ family
relations.note: Amphitryon resists the usurper who intends to kill him, Megara, and the children.

relations.myth: Lyssa drives Heracles mad and endangers Amphitryon
relations.note: Lyssa’s attack on Heracles indirectly causes his family’s massacre and nearly costs Amphitryon his life.

relations.myth: Trophonius builds Amphitryon’s Theban bridal chamber
relations.note: Regional tradition credits Trophonius and Agamedes with constructing the couple’s chamber.

relations.myth: Agamedes builds Amphitryon’s Theban bridal chamber
relations.note: Regional tradition credits Agamedes and Trophonius with constructing the couple’s chamber.

relations.myth: Antenor helps Amphitryon ignite Alcmene’s pyre
relations.note: Antenor assists Amphitryon in bringing fire against Alcmene in the pyre scene.

relations.myth: Alcmene recounts Heracles’ birth to Iole
relations.note: The aged Alcmene tells Iole about her obstructed labor and Galanthis’ intervention.

relations.myth: The Pharmacides obstruct Alcmene’s labor
relations.note: Hera’s regional agents prevent Alcmene’s delivery until Historis tricks them.
